results.summary_before: This design is a digital tremolo modulation controller intended for guitar pedal applications, generating a PWM signal that can be filtered into an analog control voltage. It uses a counter and comparator to produce the PWM waveform. The modulation rate is controlled by the input pins. It is notable for its simple implementation of a classic audio effect.
results.summary: PolyTrig is a compact ASIC-oriented digital waveform synthesis core implemented in Verilog. It generates multiple waveform types including sine, cosine, tangent and cotangent approximations, triangle, sawtooth, square and rectified sine using LUT-based signal reconstruction. The architecture uses quarter-wave LUT optimization with symmetry and phase transformations, and supports NCO-style waveform generation. Waveform selection and runtime configuration are controlled through the TinyTapeout input interface, and a cocotb verification environment is included.

results.summary_before: This project is a minimal 32-bit RV32I RISC-V processor core based on the bit-serial SERV architecture, which trades throughput for very small area by processing one bit per clock cycle. It is designed for low-resource applications and is compatible with an FPGA project from BGM infrastructure. The core is implemented in Verilog and is intended for ASIC implementation. It is notable for its extremely compact design suitable for Tiny Tapeout.
results.summary: This project implements a minimal 32-bit RISC-V processor core (RV32I) using the bit-serial SERV architecture, processing one bit per clock cycle. It is optimized for area efficiency in ASIC implementation. The core connects to external SPI flash memory for program storage and can drive optional LEDs on GPIO pins. It is implemented in Verilog.

results.summary_before: TinyMOA is a RISC-V CPU based on TinyQV with an integrated SRAM-based compute-in-memory accelerator for analog matrix multiplications. It is designed for edge AI inference, combining a bit-serial processor with analog MAC operations. The accelerator uses SRAM cells for analog computation, and the CPU controls data flow and results. No silicon test results are provided.
results.summary: TeenySPU is a 4-bit spatial processing unit implemented in Verilog that uses a spatial instruction set architecture. Operation codes are provided on the high four input bits and data loading multiplexer codes on the low four input bits. Its 4-bit inputs, bidirectional pins and outputs carry Q values, operation codes, accumulator bits, board data and output values N and M. A testbench covering all programmed operations is included with the source.

results.summary: This project implements a simple MiniRISC processor using an FSM-based control unit. It fetches instructions from the ui_in pins and steps through fetch, decode, execute and write-back phases, with an accumulator register holding intermediate results and uo_out reflecting the ACC value or operation result. The design is intended to demonstrate a minimal RISC-like processor synthesized for Tiny Tapeout and verified through simulation and hardware testing. A cocotb testbench is provided for verification.

No external hardware is required beyond the simulator's switches and 7-segment display.
results.summary: This Wokwi project implements a small combinational logic block. NOT gates are connected to inputs a and b, an OR gate to inputs c and d, an XNOR gate to inputs e and f, and an XOR gate to inputs g and h. Its outputs on uo[0], uo[1], uo[5], uo[6] and uo[7] reflect these gate results. It is tested by setting the inputs and checking the outputs against expected combinations.

results.summary: This design is a small frequency divider built from D flip-flops. It is activated by driving input0 high. The output produces a lower frequency than the input, dividing the 10 kHz clock. It is implemented in Wokwi and can be tested by observing the output frequency.
